jurisdictions.structure_note: All tracked taxes are federal and the same in every Land: income and capital gains tax (EStG), inheritance tax (ErbStG), withholding. The real estate tax is municipal and the real estate transfer tax (3.5% to 6.5%) is set by the Länder; neither is a tracked tax (PwC Germany Other taxes, last reviewed 30 Jun 2025). No regions needed.

All tracked taxes are national: income tax and surcharges, flat tax on capital gains, IFI, inheritance tax, withholding. Local property and housing taxes are not tracked (PwC France Other taxes, last reviewed 5 Jun 2025). No regions needed.

National: capital gains (26%), IVAFE and IVIE, inheritance tax, withholding. Income tax only has a regional surcharge (1.23% to 3.33%, set by each region) and a municipal one (0% to 0.9%), stored as the range on the national income row (PwC Italy, last reviewed 19 Aug 2025). Regions not created: they would differ only on that surcharge; ask Hentus whether he wants the 20 regions.

The tracked taxes are national (income tax, 28% on capital gains, stamp duty on inheritances, AIMI, withholding). The autonomous regions of the Azores and Madeira set their own VAT rates and incentive regimes (Deloitte, Portugal Highlights 2026); whether they also set a lower income tax scale is not stated by PwC or Deloitte. To verify before deciding on regions.

rates.note: Regional tax; the state default scale (used where a region sets none) runs from 0.2% to 3.5% above €10,695,996.06, after the state exemption of €700,000 (PwC, last reviewed 30 Jun 2024). Each region's own row is the one the report uses. NOT ONE RATE: headline = the top band.

Cantonal tax. Example, canton of Zurich basic scale for a single person: 0% to CHF 80,000, then 0.05% rising to 0.30% above CHF 3,262,000, before the municipal multiplier (PwC, last reviewed 27 Jun 2024). Each canton's own row is the one the report uses. NOT ONE RATE: headline = the Zurich top rate.

Regional tax; the state default scale (used where a region sets none) runs from 0.2% to 3.5% above €10,695,996.06, after the state exemption of €700,000 (PwC, last reviewed 30 Jun 2025). Each region's own row is the one the report uses. NOT ONE RATE: headline = the top band.

Cantonal tax. Example, canton of Zurich basic scale for a single person: 0% to CHF 80,000, then 0.05% rising to 0.30% above CHF 3,262,000, before the municipal multiplier (PwC, last reviewed 8 Oct 2025). Each canton's own row is the one the report uses. NOT ONE RATE: headline = the Zurich top rate.

treaties.note: Signed in Brussels on 27 Apr 2006, in force 10 Sep 2015; protocol signed 14 Jul 2009, in force 22 Jun 2016 (Belgium's list of covered tax agreements in its MLI position deposited with the OECD, entry 77). Treaty text: https://src.gov.sc/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/DTABelgium.pdf. Rates on payments FROM Belgium (PwC Belgium WHT table, last reviewed 10 Sep 2026): dividends 0/5/15%, interest 5/10%, royalties 5%. Rates on payments from Seychelles not yet read, so the WHT fields stay empty.

gaps.detail: Belgium's tax-haven lists (art. 307 CIR 92 reporting: the art. 179 AR/CIR 92 low-tax list, the EU list and the Global Forum ratings) are published by SPF Finances behind a CAPTCHA that blocks automated reading, also in archived copies; the e-Justice copy of the royal decree stopped being updated in 2003.
gaps.where_to_get: Open https://fin.belgium.be (Entreprises > International > Paradis fiscaux), download the current list of states for the payments declaration (Excel or PDF), save it in PDFs/ and tell Claude whether Mauritius (and Seychelles) is listed.

gaps.detail: Belgium is not in the Knight Frank Wealth Report 2026 Databank (only the larger markets are listed).
gaps.where_to_get: Another published count of individuals with US$30m+ (e.g. UBS Global Wealth Report country tables, Altrata). Save the page in PDFs/ and tell Claude.
